title: AI’s Rising Cybersecurity Risk
summary: AI security risk and a cautious Strategy reentry.
assessment: The cash-reserve repair is verified and the new Strategy entry has favorable interim returns. Cybersecurity risk is credible, but attributing a particular exploit to AI is unproven, and the closed-versus-open model framing overlooks existing defensive tools. The three-year investment thesis is still open.

claims.claim: War depletion increases U.S. strategic vulnerability.
claims.reason: Oil and interceptor depletion are separate constraints. Public transponder data cannot count all maritime traffic, and the article’s stronger military-readiness conclusion needs stockpile, production and contingency-demand estimates. Unpopularity is not itself a measure of operational capacity.
claims.next_check: Compare official reserve series and defense production disclosures with explicit contingency requirements.

coverage_note: Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.
framework_lessons: Balance-sheet repair can improve an opportunity without eliminating asset-price risk.
Verify an incident’s cause separately from a broad technological trend.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
